title: Milk Science — Chemistry, Physical Properties, Microbiology and Composition Factors
shortDescription: Milk chemistry, physical constants, microbial quality and what changes milk composition.
genZNote: Four lenses on one liquid: chemistry, physics, microbes, and the cow. Strippings have the most fat — fun fact that's also an MCQ.

sections.heading: Milk Chemistry
bullets: Lipids: ~98% triglycerides in fat globules wrapped by MFGM (phospholipids, proteins); high short-chain fatty acids (butyric) give butter flavour and high Reichert–Meissl value.

Proteins: caseins (αs1, αs2, β, κ) form calcium-phosphate-stabilised micelles; κ-casein stabilises micelles and is cleaved by chymosin; whey proteins (β-lactoglobulin, α-lactalbumin) are heat-sensitive.
Lactose: reducing disaccharide; Maillard browning with proteins on heating; lactose crystallisation in condensed milk causes sandiness.
Minerals: colloidal calcium phosphate; enzymes: alkaline phosphatase (pasteurization indicator), lipase, lactoperoxidase, catalase, plasmin; vitamins A, B2, B12.

sections.heading: Milk Microbiology and Composition Factors
bullets: Raw milk is nearly sterile in a healthy udder; contamination comes from teats, equipment, water, air and handling. Spoilage: Lactococcus, coliforms, psychrotrophs; pathogens: Salmonella, Listeria, E. coli, Brucella, Mycobacterium bovis; thermoduric survivors of pasteurization (Micrococcus, Bacillus).
Quality tests: SPC, coliform count, MBRT (methylene blue reduction time), resazurin test, somatic cell count (> 2–5 lakh/mL indicates mastitis).

Composition factors: species and breed (Jersey high fat), individual animal, stage of lactation (colostrum is protein/immunoglobulin rich), feed and season, age, milking interval and completeness (strippings are fat rich), mastitis and other disease.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Milk science integrates the chemistry, physical constants, microbial quality and biological factors that determine milk behaviour in processing.

commonTraps: Do not say whey proteins are heat stable.
